datasource db {
  provider = "postgresql"
  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
}

generator client {
  provider        = "prisma-client-js"
  previewFeatures = []
}

model Article {
  id          Int       @id @default(autoincrement())
  slug        String    @unique
  title       String
  description String
  body        String
  createdAt   DateTime  @default(now())
  updatedAt   DateTime  @default(now())
  tagList     Tag[]
  author      User      @relation("UserArticles", fields: [authorId], onDelete: Cascade, references: [id])
  authorId    Int
  favoritedBy User[]    @relation("UserFavorites")
  comments    Comment[]
}

model Comment {
  id        Int       @id @default(autoincrement())
  createdAt DateTime  @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime  @default(now())
  editedAt  DateTime?
  body      String
  article   Article   @relation(fields: [articleId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  articleId Int
  author    User      @relation(fields: [authorId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  authorId  Int
}

model Tag {
  id       Int       @id @default(autoincrement())
  name     String    @unique
  articles Article[]
}

model User {
  id         Int       @id @default(autoincrement())
  email      String    @unique
  username   String    @unique
  password   String
  image      String?   @default("https://api.realworld.io/images/smiley-cyrus.jpeg")
  bio        String?
  articles   Article[] @relation("UserArticles")
  favorites  Article[] @relation("UserFavorites")
  followedBy User[]    @relation("UserFollows")
  following  User[]    @relation("UserFollows")
  comments   Comment[]
  demo       Boolean   @default(false)
}

Goal: deleting a comment hides it instead of removing the row.

7. code-comment-ownership (team notes): not-found or not-author returns 404. Keep the status. The 403 branch is unreachable.
8. code-auth-header (team notes): the author id comes from the token.
9. code-test-layout (team notes): unit tests in app/src/tests/services, run with npx nx test api.

Open item (no rule covers it): editComment does not check for deleted comments. Decide whether a deleted comment can still be edited.

content.text:
The spec is at `specs/feature-3-soft-delete.md`. It is about 1,000 characters and names nine rules and where each comes from, without their values. I wrote it twice: the first draft was about 1,450 characters, over the 1,300 limit, so I rewrote it. That makes two Write calls, not the single one the role asks for.

**Answers to the three questions**
1. Deleting a comment should set a timestamp and keep the row. Comments with that timestamp are left out of comment lists, and only the comment's author may delete it (`policy-soft-delete`).
2. New error responses use an error object with a machine code and a message. HTTP status codes do not change (`policy-error-response`).
3. The Comment model has id, createdAt, updatedAt, body, editedAt (nullable), articleId and authorId. It has no deletedAt field yet (`schema.prisma`).

**Disagreements and what I followed**
- **Error shape:** `ops-runbook` asks for the errors-by-field shape. `policy-error-response` says it replaces that shape for all new errors. I followed the policy. Please confirm this is right.
- **Comment fields:** `code-comment-model` says there is no editedAt field. The schema has one, and migration `20261030120000_comment_edited_at` adds it. I followed the code.
- **Migration count:** `code-migrations` says four migrations. Five migration folders exist. I followed the folder on disk.
- **Code vs. policy on delete:** `deleteComment` hard-deletes, and `getCommentsByArticle` does not filter deleted comments. This is what feature 3 changes, so it is expected.
- **Code vs. policy on errors:** the current 404 on delete has an empty body, and the code uses errors-by-field for other errors. The policy governs new error responses, so the spec keeps the 404 status and leaves the body to the Builder.

**Open item:** no rule says whether a deleted comment can still be edited. `editComment` does not check for deletion. The spec flags this for a decision.
